articles.title: Mississauga's leading candidates face off for final time, with focus on arts facility, police funding
articles.summary: Mississauga's leading mayoral candidates took a more collegial approach to Thursday's debate than in past face-offs, responding to a mix of challenging and light-hearted questions from residents.

articles.title: E-scooter rider seriously injured in Brampton crash
articles.summary: A male e-scooter rider has been taken to hospital with life-threatening injuries after a crash in Brampton. Police were called to Queen Street West and Mercer Drive just before 9:30 p.m. for reports of a crash. Officers say both drivers remained on the scene. articles.title: 1 injured in Brampton single vehicle crash
articles.summary: One person has been taken to hospital after a single vehicle crash in Brampton. Police were called to Gorewood Drive north of Steeles Avenue just before 9 p.m. for reports of a crash. The cause of the crash remains unknown. articles.title: Meta Centre Film Festival returns to North York for second year
articles.summary: A film festival showcasing the creativity of people living with developmental and cognitive disabilities is returning to North York for its second year. The Meta Centre Film Festival kicked off Thursday at York Woods Library Theatre. The event features a series of short films created by 25 Meta Centre clients over the past year. The […]

articles.title: Did Toronto actually fix Regent Park?
articles.summary: Billions spent. Thousands displaced. CBC's Igor Petrov goes inside Canada's biggest public housing experiment to see if the massive revitalization of Toronto's Regent Park is a successful blueprint for urban renewal — or a failed experiment.

articles.title: Man arrested after 2 alleged sexual assaults at Scarborough school: Toronto police
articles.summary: A 24-year-old man allegedly posed as a grade 12 student and sexually assaulted two students at a Toronto school last month, police say.

articles.title: Supreme Court to hear challenge of legislation for Ontario Place redevelopment
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of Canada plans to hear arguments Thursday from a coalition challenging the constitutionality of legislation that smooths the way for major changes at Ontario Place. The Crown and Ontario's attorney general are urging the court to dismiss the case.

articles.title: Cyclists delay province's bike lane removal start in Toronto, 2 arrested
articles.summary: Cyclists in Toronto delayed work by the province to remove bike lanes on a stretch of Bloor Street W. temporarily this week with a protest that began Tuesday evening and led to two arrests.
